correctness.rationale: Painless Ron–Shen equations reduce even arbitrary complex Bessel duals to two-site fibers. The strict coefficient-order fiber optimization proves the unique \(L^1\) extremizer, cap feasibility, exact support minimum, integral expression and threshold behavior. Differentiation and local asymptotics provide the logarithmic and fractional coefficients. The standalone checker completed 9913 rational vertex LP cases, 51 independent integral comparisons, and 36 support-measure checks. None of these finite checks substitutes for the analytic proof.

evidence: Theorem 2.7 of Díaz Martín et al. characterizes unrestricted minimizers as pointwise weights supported only at maxima of the analysis window; with cap below \(\beta2^r\) the maximizing-only dual violates the cap on positive-measure fibers.

The constrained theorem must instead place nonzero mass on the smaller coefficient on such fibers; it has strictly increased \(L^1\)-norm and support, which cannot be inferred as a special case of the unrestricted equality characterization.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Existing unrestricted results imply exactly the cap \(T\ge\beta2^r\) plateau. For \(\beta\max\{1,2^{r-1}\}\le T<\beta2^r\) the unrestricted minimum is not peak-feasible; a distinct constrained optimization is required. The nonanalytic tent cusp and fractional exponent arise from its new cutoff. The generic convex-optimization framework can in principle numerically find these solutions but does not state or mathematically imply their exact values without further reasoning.

value.rationale: An essential-supremum cap on the synthesis window directly bounds pointwise amplification of ℓ1 coefficient errors; the resulting optimal norm/support tradeoff is a meaningful constraint in time-frequency synthesis design. The result gives the exact feasible cap, a unique dual, sharp support cost, strict convexity and exponent-dependent logarithmic/fractional boundary behavior, not a mere textbook restatement or arbitrarily chosen finite cutoff.
